text_blocks.snippet: Long COVID, also known as post-COVID-19 condition, can begin anytime from weeks to months after the initial SARS-CoV-2 infection. Symptoms can emerge, persist, resolve, and then reappear over time. The World Health Organization (WHO) began studying this condition in 2020, when reports of persistent symptoms emerged following the first wave of the pandemic.

text_blocks.snippet: The exact causes of long COVID, a condition where symptoms persist or develop after a COVID-19 infection, are still being investigated. However, several potential mechanisms have been proposed, including:

list.title: Immune response:
list.snippet: The body's immune system may continue to attack the virus or its remnants even after the initial infection has cleared, leading to inflammation and damage in various organs.

list.title: Viral persistence:
list.snippet: The virus may remain in the body for an extended period, causing ongoing symptoms.

list.title: Autoimmune response:
list.snippet: The body's immune system may mistakenly attack its own healthy tissues, resulting in long-term health problems.

list.title: Microvascular damage:
list.snippet: The virus can damage small blood vessels, leading to organ dysfunction and inflammation.

list.title: Gut microbiome disruption:
list.snippet: Changes in the gut microbiome composition may contribute to the development of long COVID symptoms.

list.title: Pre-existing health conditions:
list.snippet: Individuals with underlying health conditions may be more susceptible to developing long COVID.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that long COVID is a complex condition with multiple potential causes. Further research is needed to fully understand its underlying mechanisms and develop effective treatments.
